_comment: Installed-cost and structural-load model for the ShieldLab cost/material optimizer. For each shielding material: 'installed_cost_usd_per_m3' is the delivered-and-installed cost of one cubic metre of the finished barrier (material + fabrication + fixing/placement labour), the natural unit for a wall built by volume; the optimizer multiplies it by the required thickness to get cost per m2 of wall. Structural areal load (kg/m2) is taken from density in materials.json. THESE ARE REPRESENTATIVE 2026 INTERNATIONAL ESTIMATES AND ARE VOLATILE AND REGIONAL — replace every figure with a local contractor quotation before relying on a ranking. Edit this file freely; the optimizer reads it live.

_units.installed_cost: USD per cubic metre of finished barrier

_disclaimer: Costs are order-of-magnitude planning estimates for RELATIVE comparison between materials, not a quotation. Lead and lead-glass in particular vary widely with sheet gauge, fixing detail and supplier. Always confirm with local quotes and a structural engineer for the areal load.
_sources: Lead/steel commodity prices 2025-2026 (LME/producer) plus typical fabrication+fixing; concrete/barite/brick from general construction cost data (RSMeans-class ready-mix, heavy-aggregate premium ~4-6x ordinary, and masonry labour). Ranges given per material; point value is a mid estimate.

lead.cost_basis: sheet lead ~8 USD/kg installed (raw ~3.5 + fabrication/fixing/overlap) x 11350 kg/m3
lead.labour_note: Needs backing, overlapped joints and fixing detail; specialist install. Very thin, very heavy, very costly per m3 but you use little thickness.

concrete.labour_note: Cheapest bulk shielding; needs the most space and adds large structural load.

barite_concrete.cost_basis: barite (barytes) aggregate ~4-6x ordinary aggregate + specialist placement to avoid segregation
barite_concrete.labour_note: Compact high-density vault walls; ~40% thinner than ordinary concrete for the same attenuation but several times the cost. Placement quality-critical.

brick.cost_basis: solid clay brick + labour-intensive masonry laying
brick.labour_note: Regionally available structural option; labour dominates. Verify mortar joints / void fraction — a real wall attenuates less than solid brick.

steel.cost_basis: structural/plate steel ~2.7 USD/kg installed x 7800 kg/m3
steel.labour_note: Compact, structural, but heavy and expensive; used where space is tight and load path exists (e.g. doors).

gypsum.cost_basis: gypsum board / plaster; low density -> weak shielding, cheap
gypsum.labour_note: Minor attenuation only; useful as a finish layer, rarely a primary shield.

plate_glass.labour_note: Viewing only; weak shielding. For a shielded window use lead glass and specify by mm Pb equivalence.

lead_glass.cost_basis: leaded viewing glass, typically quoted per m2 by mm Pb equivalence; converted at ~5200 kg/m3
lead_glass.labour_note: Specialist viewing windows; specify by lead equivalence (mm Pb) at the working kVp, framed to match the wall's Pb equivalent.

steel_lead_note._note: This is a placeholder key ignored by the optimizer (it only reads materials that also exist in materials.json).
